definitions.explanation: A situation that was not predicted or planned for. Used in formal contexts when discussing risk management, emergency preparedness, and crisis response.

examples.japanese: {不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}に{備|そな}える。
{不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}が{起|お}きた{場合|ばあい}の{対応|たいおう}{手順|てじゅん}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: We confirmed the response procedures in case of an emergency.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{出張|しゅっちょう}{中|ちゅう}に{不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}が{発生|はっせい}しても{対処|たいしょ}できるよう、{保険|ほけん}に{加入|かにゅう}した。
examples.english: I took out insurance so I can deal with unexpected situations during business trips abroad.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal expression used in risk management, business planning, and official communications. Often appears in safety manuals, disaster preparedness documents, and contracts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}に{備|そな}える (to prepare for contingencies)
- {不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}が{発生|はっせい}する (an unexpected situation occurs)
- {不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}に{陥|おちい}る (to fall into an unforeseen situation)
- {不測|ふそく}の{事態|じたい}に{対処|たいしょ}する (to deal with an emergency)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {緊急事態|きんきゅうじたい}: emergency — specifically an urgent crisis requiring immediate action
- {非常事態|ひじょうじたい}: state of emergency — an officially declared crisis
- {想定外|そうていがい}: beyond expectations — something that was not anticipated, less formal
